question: Device-ness is decided at the shim, and today a shim is granted by disk discovery: a class-space probes/ folder IS the registration (ground_loop/discovery.py). The 2026-08-12 ruling splits a probe's definition (code) from its runtime data (the .cairn tree) and gives held tools and machines their own instance folders. So where a probe is DEFINED stops being evidence of anything about its holder — which leaves discovery without a basis. What grants a shim now?
whats_beyond: MEASURED 2026-08-12: cairn/base carries 4 probes and is therefore ON THE DEVICE ROSTER — the tool drawer is a device, pulsed by the heartbeat, because probes/ is the sole registration path. Under the four rungs (tools, machines, devices, device instances) that is a category error, and it is not an accident of base: today a TOOL CAN ONLY BE WATCHED BY IMPERSONATING A DEVICE, since there is no other way to get a probe fired. The tools/ layout supplies the missing address (a tool's probe data hangs off its holder's instance, fired by its holder's shim), but nothing yet says which folders confer device-ness and which are held parts. Candidate bases, none ruled: an explicit declaration in the charter; the presence of an instance directory; a shim class existing; or the rung being derived rather than declared. The last is the one that fits Law 4 and is the hardest.
source: The tools/machines/devices/instances conversation, 2026-08-11 evening into 2026-08-12. Filed under decisions/2026-08-12-tools-machines-devices-instances.json, whose `registration_now_has_two_sources` finding this is.
